World.definition: The true, data-generating model. Contains everything, including twists.

Variable.definition: Any column: a Latent or an Attribute.

Latent.definition: An attitude or outcome in the researcher's model (feedback, self-efficacy, achievement…). One column each.

Attribute.definition: A student or school descriptor that EMM searches over (gender, school type…).

Level.definition: Student or School. School-level values are shared by all students in the school.

Root.definition: A Variable with no incoming arrows. Specified by a Distribution.

Child.definition: A Variable with incoming arrows. Specified by a Recipe.

Distribution.definition: Proportions (categorical) or mean + SD (continuous) for a Root.

Recipe.definition: Intercept + noise SD for a Child; slopes live on its incoming arrows.

Derived.definition: A value computed from the World, never typed: a Child's mean and SD, total effects.

Arrow.definition: A direct cause with a slope.

Level Shift.definition: An Arrow from an Attribute into a Latent. The attribute is added. Moves averages, not slopes.

Twist.definition: A planted subgroup: a slope change on an existing Arrow, under a Condition. The attribute is multiplied.
Twist.amendment: Design: Δ per value relative to the arrow's baseline; twists on different attributes add.

Condition.definition: Which students a Twist applies to: one attribute equal to one value.

Decoy.definition: An Attribute that affects nothing. Tests for false positives.

Seed.definition: Makes generation reproducible. World + Seed = one exact Dataset.

True Quantities.definition: Direct effects, total effects, means, SDs and standardized coefficients, computed from the World.

Dataset.definition: One row per student. Synthetic (has truth) or Real (no truth).

Frame.definition: Which rows and schools a Dataset contains, and how they were selected.

Researcher's Model.definition: Latents + Arrows between them. No attributes, no twists. What gets fitted, with OLS.

Residualization.definition: Clicking a node to show its total effect. Triangle or chain case.
Residualization.amendment: Design D4: subtract X's model-implied total effect from every descendant of X used as a regressor.

Search Space.definition: Attributes + binning + depth + minimum sizes + optional filter.

Analysis Run.definition: Dataset + model + settings + search space + EMM settings → ranked Subgroups.

Subgroup.definition: A description (e.g. school_type = rich) and the students it covers.

Fragile.definition: A subgroup with fewer than 25 schools.
Fragile.amendment: Design T5: tiers use effective schools (schools with ≥3 subgroup members): < 20 Unreliable, 20–49 Fragile, ≥ 50 OK. The current preset also reports the < 25 nominal-schools rule.

Bootstrap.definition: School-cluster resampling, everything recomputed inside each replicate.

Report.definition: Differing paths, intervals, equations, means, SDs, meaning, share of variance.

Scorecard.definition: Hits, misses, false positives, step checks. Synthetic only.

Experiment.definition: Runs that vary one thing at a time.

Provenance.definition: Everything needed to regenerate any number.

Unreliable.definition: Fewer than 20 effective schools: intervals shown greyed out (design T5).

Unstable.definition: A finding whose hit rate across replications lies between 0.2 and 0.8: it would flip on reseeding (design T5).

T1 Structural truth.definition: The World's slopes per cell: direct and total effects.

T2 Causal target.definition: The π-weighted average effect over the analysed (sub)population.

T3 Step estimand.definition: What this exact model, on this exact filtered and transformed population, converges to.

Method preset.definition: current = faithful replica of the researcher's pipeline; recommended = research-backed fixes (design T1).

Null World.definition: The same World with every twist removed; its replications measure false positives directly (design T3).

MCSE.definition: Monte Carlo standard error: the uncertainty of a rate estimated from a finite number of replications.

Common metric.definition: Variables standardized once on the full sample; subgroup slopes are compared on that scale (design D2).
